user.text: Add view transitions to this product gallery app. When navigating from the grid to a product detail page, the product image should smoothly morph between the thumbnail and the large detail image using a shared element transition. Page navigations should slide directionally. Suspense loading states should transition smoothly from skeleton to content. All animations must respect the user's prefers-reduced-motion preference.

history.assistant:
I added all three animations and the reduced-motion handling. The typecheck and production build pass, and both pages load, but I haven't watched the animations run in a browser, so how they look is still untested.

**How it works** (following the view-transitions guide that ships with Next 16.4):

- **Image morph:** the grid thumbnail and the large detail image share the same name, `product-image-<slug>`. On navigation they morph into each other over 400ms with a slight blur partway through. The large image renders outside the page's loading boundary so it appears at the same moment as the navigation; that's what lets it pair with the thumbnail.
- **Directional slides:** grid links are tagged `nav-forward` and "← Back to products" is tagged `nav-back`. A new wrapper, `app/PageTransition.tsx`, wraps both pages: forward slides content left, back slides it right, fading and moving 60px. The browser's own back/forward buttons don't carry a direction, so they skip the slide; the image morph still plays.
- **Loading states:** skeletons fade and slide down out of view (150ms), then the real content fades and slides up into place. On the detail page this runs when the product info arrives (it takes about 100ms). The home page grid is wrapped the same way, but it never actually shows a loading state today, so nothing plays there.
- **Reduced motion:** when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set, every view-transition animation is set to 0s, so content just swaps instantly. The existing skeleton pulse is turned off too.
- I also let clicks pass through to the page while an animation is running, so they aren't lost.

**Checks:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passed (exit 0).
- `npx next build` passed (exit 0): `/` built as a static page and `/product/[slug]` as a dynamic one.
- With `next start`, `/` returned 200, the detail page rendered the product name and back link, and an unknown product returned 404. My command to stop the server also ended its own shell (signal 15), but the server did stop.

**Side effects of the build:** Next reformatted `tsconfig.json` and added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to its `include` list, which it does on every build. It also created `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts` and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, which are uncommitted. Your existing changes to `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are untouched.

Browsers without support for the View Transitions API still navigate normally, just without animation.

With `default="none"` and no `share` prop, the pair silently stops morphing. 125 126 ```css filename="app/globals.css" 127 ::view-transition-group(.morph) { 128 animation-duration: 400ms; 129 } 130 ::view-transition-image-pair(.morph) { 131 animation-name: via-blur; 132 } 133 @keyframes via-blur { 134 30% { 135 filter: blur(3px); 136 } 137 } 138 ``` 139 140 The blur hides pixel-level interpolation artifacts during the transition. export default async function CollectionPage({ params }) {
  const { slug } = await params

  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<CollectionGridSkeleton />}>
      <ViewTransition
        key={slug}
        name="collection-content"
        share="auto"
        enter="auto"
        default="none"
      >
        <CollectionGrid slug={slug} />
      </ViewTransition>
    </Suspense>
  )
}
```

The `share="auto"` and `enter="auto"` props tell React to use its default crossfade animation. The `name` prop gives the container an identity so React knows what to animate. The navigation triggers the transition; the `key={slug}` change makes React treat the old and new content as an exit/enter pair (activating `share`) instead of an in-place update.

If we click between photographer tabs, the grid crossfades. The tab bar and surrounding layout do not move. Only the photo grid transitions between states.

## Next steps

You now know how to use view transitions to communicate meaning during navigation. Shared elements communicate continuity across routes. Suspense reveals animate loading handoffs. Directional slides encode navigation history. Crossfades signal content changes within the same location.

Each pattern answers a different question for the user:

| Pattern                | What it communicates            |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Shared element (morph) | "Same thing, going deeper"      |
| Suspense reveal        | "Data loaded"                   |
| Directional slide      | "Going forward / coming back"   |
| Same-route crossfade   | "Same place, different content" |

For API details and more patterns:

- [`useRouter`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), which also supports `transitionTypes` in `push()` and `replace()`

The `share="auto"` and `enter="auto"` props tell React to use its default crossfade animation. The `name` prop gives the container an identity so React knows what to animate. The navigation triggers the transition; the `key={slug}` change makes React treat the old and new content as an exit/enter pair (activating `share`) instead of an in-place update.

If we click between photographer tabs, the grid crossfades. The tab bar and surrounding layout do not move. Only the photo grid transitions between states.

## Next steps

You now know how to use view transitions to communicate meaning during navigation. Shared elements communicate continuity across routes. Suspense reveals animate loading handoffs. Directional slides encode navigation history. Crossfades signal content changes within the same location.

Each pattern answers a different question for the user:

| Pattern                | What it communicates            |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Shared element (morph) | "Same thing, going deeper"      |
| Suspense reveal        | "Data loaded"                   |
| Directional slide      | "Going forward / coming back"   |
| Same-route crossfade   | "Same place, different content" |
